title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: In Niger, the S4Nut programme drove major progress in building climate‑resilient local economic systems, with vulnerable producers adopting drought‑tolerant varieties, improved soil and water management techniques, and sustainable farming practices that stabilised yields in highly degraded environments. Households strengthened their food and nutrition security through diversified production, better storage and increased use of nutrient‑rich crops, reducing reliance on negative coping strategies during lean periods. Preparedness for hazards improved as community observatories, women’s groups and local authorities collaborated to anticipate floods and activate timely protective measures, supporting more resilient food systems. . Floods, droughts and market disruptions repeatedly threaten household food and nutrition security in Niger, ICSP strengthens community early‑warning and contingency‑planning systems so high‑risk communities can anticipate hazards and take timely action to protect their livelihoods and food supplies.
